verdict.rationale: WorkOS documents first-party M2M applications that issue API access credentials for programmatic, non-human access. AuthKit is also a spec-compatible OAuth authorization server for securing MCP servers, so agents could receive their own machine credentials rather than borrowing a human's. However, nothing ties RBAC permissions to these machine identities, describes per-agent least-privilege scoping, or covers revocation. Its own MCP server explicitly acts with the same data access as the human. Missing for 10: documented per-agent machine identities, narrowly scoped permissions or OAuth scopes for M2M clients, an instant credential revocation mechanism, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give each agent its own least-privilege machine identity with narrowly scoped permissions and instant revocation, instead of sharing a human's credentials

citations.quote: M2M applications are commonly used to provide API access credentials to customers or partners, allowing them to programmatically access your APIs
WorkOS and AuthKit can provide a secure way to manage access to your MCP server with minimal effort.
AuthKit, which is a spec-compatible OAuth authorization server.
